delay_description: Existing tenant — tenancy must end before going live

trigger_phrases.phrase: Existing tenant/occupant not due to move out for several months
Legally unable to serve notice — sitting tenants can only leave through natural turnover or on sale of the property
Tenant has verbally agreed to leave but formal notice has not yet been served
Vendor let the property to tenants unexpectedly, creating condition and availability uncertainty
Converting an existing long-let tenancy into a short-let

typical_timeline.notes: Vacate dates ranged from about five weeks (notice period already running) to six-plus months (rolling HMO-style departures); most leads pointed to roughly a season (2-3 months) before the property would actually be empty.

what_leads_focus_on_while_waiting.concern: Confirming the exact date the tenant/occupant will actually vacate
Whether they can legally compel or time the tenant's departure at all
Coordinating the STL go-live date with seasonal demand once the property is free
What condition the property will be in once the tenant leaves
Parallel financial/mortgage decisions that also need to land before the property can be relet

how_to_handle_in_meeting.acknowledge_phrase: It would definitely be within September... middle of September, probably latest, we could probably go live.
how_to_handle_in_meeting.timeline_question: Once your tenant/occupant is actually out, is there a firm date for that yet, or is it still an estimate — and is notice formally served, or just discussed verbally?
how_to_handle_in_meeting.reframe_approach: Treat the tenant's departure as a fixed external date to plan backward from, not an open-ended 'someday' — pin a go-live window immediately after it and show what onboarding looks like in that window.
how_to_handle_in_meeting.how_to_keep_engaged: Agree a specific follow-up call tied to the known or expected vacate date (not a vague 'touch base'), and offer to start the paperwork/analyser work now so nothing but the vacate date is left to wait on.
how_to_handle_in_meeting.what_to_write_to_monday: Log the tenant/occupant type, the vacate date (confirmed or estimated) and whether formal notice has been served, so the pipeline reflects a dated trigger rather than a generic nurture status.

do_not_attempt_offer_because: The property is physically occupied by someone else, so Stayful cannot take possession, photograph, furnish, or list it — and in HMO/licensed-tenancy cases the lead may have no legal mechanism to accelerate the tenant's departure at all, making any signing-deadline discount pointless until a real vacate date exists.
